flags.detail: The prompt and part (A) direct students to 'the excerpt,' and the sample's (A) attributes specific claims to it (land grants, redemption payments to the government stretched over almost fifty years), but no excerpt is included in the material. The excerpt's content, author, date and purpose therefore cannot be verified, and it is impossible to confirm that the sample's (B) choice (the Crimean War) does not violate the 'do not use a development the excerpt names' restriction—especially since the prompt stem itself names the Crimean defeat. The sample's own historical statements (49-year redemption payments; Crimean War 1853–56 lost to Britain and France; minimal railways; serf-conscript army; later creation of a Duma) are otherwise accurate.

The prompt says 'Using the excerpt,' and the sample (A) attributes specific claims to it (emancipation carried out by landlord-dominated local commissions; serfs given land but only limited freedom), but no excerpt or credit line is included in the material. The sample's characterization of the source therefore cannot be verified against the document, and students would have no text to work from. (The historical content of the sample's (A), (B) and (C) is otherwise accurate, if vague.)
